cl_opi_withdrawal_alpha2.q: Do clonidine or lofexidine help with opioid withdrawal?
cl_opi_withdrawal_alpha2.short: Yes: compared with a dummy pill, fewer people had bad withdrawal and more finished treatment.
cl_opi_withdrawal_alpha2.but: Only three small, old trials, mostly in hospital, and none with people coming off fentanyl.
how: Three trials gave people coming off heroin or methadone either the medicine or a dummy pill, picked by chance.
Bad withdrawal happened to about 19 in 100 on the medicine and about 59 in 100 on the dummy pill.
About 56 in 100 finished treatment on the medicine, against 29 in 100 on the dummy pill.
The medicine made some people sleepy or dizzy and lowered their blood pressure.

cl_opi_withdrawal_alpha2_vs_methadone.q: Is clonidine as good as slowly cutting down methadone for coming off opioids?
cl_opi_withdrawal_alpha2_vs_methadone.short: About as many people finished, but clonidine-type medicines caused more dizziness and low blood pressure.
cl_opi_withdrawal_alpha2_vs_methadone.but: The trials were small and some were badly run, so the answer could change.
how: Twelve trials compared clonidine-type medicines with methadone given in slowly shrinking amounts.
Withdrawal felt about as bad overall, but it started and ended sooner with clonidine-type medicines.
Low blood pressure and other side effects were about twice as common as with methadone.
Neither way took away all the aches, bad sleep and worry.

cl_opi_withdrawal_buprenorphine.q: Does buprenorphine help people get through opioid withdrawal better than clonidine?
cl_opi_withdrawal_buprenorphine.short: Yes: more people finished withdrawal treatment with buprenorphine than with clonidine or lofexidine.
cl_opi_withdrawal_buprenorphine.but: These trials happened before fentanyl was common, and two stopped early, which can make results look better.
how: Fourteen trials put people coming off opioids, mostly heroin, on buprenorphine or on clonidine or lofexidine, by chance.
About 72 in 100 finished treatment on buprenorphine, against about 45 in 100 on the other medicines.
Withdrawal was milder on average, and people stayed in treatment longer.
Side effects were about as common but different: headache and constipation with buprenorphine, dizziness with clonidine.

cl_opi_withdrawal_buprenorphine_vs_metha.q: Is buprenorphine better than slowly cutting down methadone for coming off opioids?
cl_opi_withdrawal_buprenorphine_vs_metha.short: They worked about the same: similar numbers of people finished withdrawal treatment with each.
cl_opi_withdrawal_buprenorphine_vs_metha.but: Only six small trials, mostly in hospitals or a prison.
how: Six trials compared buprenorphine with methadone given in slowly shrinking amounts.
About 55 in 100 finished on buprenorphine and about 53 in 100 on methadone.
The trials could not show whether withdrawal felt different with one or the other.

cl_fent_withdrawal_severity.q: Is withdrawal from fentanyl worse than withdrawal from heroin?
cl_fent_withdrawal_severity.short: In one study, people coming off fentanyl had worse withdrawal than people coming off heroin.
cl_fent_withdrawal_severity.but: The two groups were studied ten years apart, so something other than fentanyl may explain it.
how: 30 people who had used fentanyl were compared with 103 people who had used heroin or similar drugs ten years earlier.
Both groups got the same medicine on the same research ward.
The fentanyl group's withdrawal got worse over the first days before easing, while the other group's eased from the start.
A fast heartbeat happened to 43 in 100 in the fentanyl group, against 19 in 100 in the other group.
